author: KirillSmirnov
title: Build (C++20) job fails - sccache cannot start because Azure Blob connection string URI is malformed
signature: sccache server startup failed cache storage failed to read unexpected permanent at read azbloberror code invaliduri message the requested uri does not represent any resource on the server|Configuration

failed_jobs.name: Build (C++20, non-blocking) / Build
failed_jobs.symptom: CMake C compiler check fails because sccache server fails to start, aborting configure

key_errors: CMake Error at /usr/share/cmake-3.28/Modules/CMakeTestCCompiler.cmake:67 (message): The C compiler "/usr/bin/cc" is not able to compile a simple test program.

sccache: error: Server startup failed: cache storage failed to read: Unexpected (permanent) at read => AzblobError { code: "InvalidUri", message: "The requested URI does not represent any resource on the server." }
root_cause: The non-blocking C++20 build job sets CMAKE_C_COMPILER_LAUNCHER/CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_LAUNCHER to sccache with an Azure Blob remote cache backend (SCCACHE_AZURE_CONNECTION_STRING/SCCACHE_AZURE_KEY_PREFIX). The sccache daemon fails to start because the blob storage URI it builds (note the double slash in 'https://ghasccacheblobs.blob.core.windows.net//sccache/...') is rejected by Azure with 'InvalidUri'. This is almost certainly caused by a misconfigured SCCACHE_AZURE_CONNECTION_STRING/key-prefix combination (an extra separator or malformed container/blob-prefix value) producing a doubled path separator, rather than a transient service outage, since the identical signature has now recurred 9 times over the past week across many unrelated PRs with the same double-slash URI pattern.
reproduction_steps: N/A - requires the CI runner's SCCACHE_AZURE_CONNECTION_STRING secret and cache endpoint; cannot be reproduced locally. To reproduce in CI, trigger the 'Build (C++20, non-blocking)' job and inspect CMakeFiles/CMakeError.log / sccache --show-stats output for the AzblobError.
recommended_actions: Inspect the SCCACHE_AZURE_KEY_PREFIX / SCCACHE_AZURE_CONNECTION_STRING configuration used by the 'Build (C++20, non-blocking)' job (likely in .github/workflows/job_build_linux_cpp20.yml or a shared composite action) for a trailing/leading slash that produces the doubled '//' segment in the blob URI.
Compare the Azure Blob prefix configuration against other build jobs (e.g. ARM64) that use sccache successfully to find the discrepancy.

Consider setting SCCACHE_IGNORE_SERVER_IO_ERROR more defensively or adding a fallback to local caching when the Azure backend is unreachable/misconfigured, so a cache misconfiguration does not fail the whole build.
Once fixed, verify by re-running the C++20 job and confirming sccache startup succeeds (no AzblobError in logs).
prevention_strategies: Add a startup self-check step that validates the sccache Azure Blob URI (e.g., a HEAD request to the configured endpoint) before the main build begins, failing fast with a clear configuration error instead of an opaque CMake compiler-detection failure. Periodically audit the SCCACHE_AZURE_* secrets/variables across workflow files to catch future URI drift. Since this is a non-blocking job, consider also alerting on sustained sccache-caused failures separately from the main merge gate.
historical_context: This exact signature (pattern 08b993dbdc18ccac) has now recurred 9 times since 2026-11-06, most recently at 2026-11-13T03:40:54Z (run 43352207166) and now again in this run. It has affected many unrelated PRs (#39563, #39717, #38204, #39578, #39262, #39034, #39101, and now #39266), confirming this is a persistent CI infrastructure/configuration defect in the C++20 non-blocking build job rather than an issue with any specific PR's code changes.
